answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted reputation that decays: every agent locks a small refundable bond before it can transact, and each honest attestation slowly raises its trust score while a failure slashes it. New identities start at zero, so a Sybil farmer must fund and age thousands of bonds before any of them matter. Picture the bond pool as a lotus pond: honest agents rise through clear water, while umber sludge — fake accounts with no past — sinks and stays visible at the bottom. The ledger becomes a haven only for identities that paid, in time and stake, to prove they are real.
